findings.obligation: B1 and B5: an ELF that cannot be read or whose GLIBC needs cannot be parsed is indeterminate, exit 2, never a pass; Y2: floor check never passes silently; falsifier: passes a file whose GLIBC needs it failed to parse
findings.observation: Probe A (R4): one file made by head -c 2000 of the bash binary, ELF magic intact. readelf -V and readelf -d both fail, links_libc is false, the loop reaches continue. Output: scanned=1 highest=GLIBC_none over_floor=0 and needs at most GLIBC_2.39, exit 0. Also line 75 is_elf read failure is a silent skip: probe B chmod 000 copy skipped with no message, scanned=2 of 3 files. A check that exits 0 with an unread file in the tree is a false pass the release gate cannot see.
findings.remediation: Test the exit status of readelf -V and readelf -d and of the magic read. Any failure counts as unreadable: write WHAT/WHY/HOW, count it, and exit 2 (never 0). Replace the process-substitution find with a check of its exit status or a captured listing, so an unreadable directory also gives exit 2. Keep exit 1 precedence only for real offenders.

findings.obligation: Falsifier of the S1 oracle: a check that passes a file whose GLIBC needs it failed to parse must fail the oracle; Y2: exit 0 with scanned work must never mask unreadable input
findings.observation: The only parse-failure case is the stripped version-needs section (script reads readelf -d fine, so the libc link branch fires). No case covers a file that readelf cannot read at all, or a file the scan user cannot read. Probe A (R4) passes that shape with exit 0, so the oracle as written would stay green on the defect in F1.
findings.remediation: Add two fixtures: a truncated ELF (magic intact, body cut after the header) expecting exit 2 and naming the file, and a non-readable file read by a non-root user inside the container (root bypasses chmod) expecting exit 2. Keep the existing stripped case. Re-review only this delta after the implementation fix.

findings.obligation: L1: the floor is a dotted numeric version; B1: a check that cannot read what it needs exits 2, never 0
findings.observation: Probe C (R4): floor argument abc gives stderr 10#abc value too great for base, stdout needs at most GLIBC_abc, exit 0. The argument is never validated before the numeric comparison, so a malformed floor passes. The release workflow passes no floor argument, so the release gate itself is not affected today; manual and oracle callers are.
findings.remediation: After the floor is chosen, require a match of ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$ and exit 2 with WHAT/WHY/HOW otherwise. Add one oracle case with a malformed floor argument expecting exit 2.

findings.obligation: Docs state the Linux minimum in user terms, true to the ADR (docs/product/architecture/adr-284 line 16: the distribution must provide WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3, which the AppImage does not bundle)
findings.observation: The line reads: Your distribution must also provide WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3, which are installed by default on most desktop Linux systems. The default-install claim is not in the ADR and no evidence in the packet supports it. Severity Low.
findings.remediation: Delete the which-are-installed-by-default clause, keep the must-provide sentence. Owner decides copy.
